components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
土 (earth) — a lump of earth; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
夬 (guài) is a loose clue; 快 kuài shares it and sounds exactly like 块.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 那个大块头轻松地举起了两百公斤的杠铃。
example.pinyin: Nàge dàkuàitóu qīngsōng de jǔqǐ le liǎngbǎi gōngjīn de gànglíng.
example.english: That big guy lifted the two-hundred-kilogram barbell with ease.
example.fact: The African bush elephant is the largest living land animal, with bulls reaching up to 6,000 kilograms — roughly the mass of a fully loaded city bus.

examples.hanzi: 他是个大块头，可是性格很温柔。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè dàkuàitóu, kěshì xìnggé hěn wēnróu.
examples.english: He's a big guy, but he has a gentle nature.

examples.hanzi: 这个大块头一进门，屋子就显得小了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàkuàitóu yī jìn mén, wūzi jiù xiǎnde xiǎo le.
examples.english: The moment this big guy walked in, the room seemed smaller.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: water draining away.
肖 (xiāo) gives the exact sound; also in 销 xiāo and 削 xuē.

example.hanzi: 他的怒气渐渐消了。
example.pinyin: Tā de nùqì jiànjiàn xiāo le.
example.english: His anger gradually faded.
example.fact: 消 is the heart of 消息 (news), 消失 (vanish), 消费 (consume), 消化 (digest) and 取消 (cancel). On its own, it means to subside, as in 肿消了, 'the swelling went down'.

examples.hanzi: 雨停了，天上的乌云慢慢消了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ tíng le, tiān shàng de wūyún mànmàn xiāo le.
examples.english: The rain stopped and the dark clouds slowly cleared away.

examples.hanzi: 我吃完饭要去散步，帮助消化。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī wán fàn yào qù sànbù, bāngzhù xiāohuà.
examples.english: After eating I will take a walk to help digestion.

components.note: 日 (sun) — light and brightness: 明, 晴, 时; 显 is something lit up and clear to see.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服显得你很年轻。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu xiǎnde nǐ hěn niánqīng.
example.english: This outfit makes you look young.
example.fact: 显得 means 'to look, to seem' and is extremely common. 显然 is 'obviously', 显示 is 'to display', and 明显 is 'clear'.

examples.hanzi: 红色的衣服显得她很精神。
examples.pinyin: Hóngsè de yīfu xiǎnde tā hěn jīngshen.
examples.english: The red clothes make her look energetic.

examples.hanzi: 他的错误很明显。
examples.pinyin: Tā de cuòwù hěn míngxiǎn.
examples.english: His mistake is obvious.

components.note: 门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.hanzi: 他给远方的朋友写信表示问候。
example.pinyin: Tā gěi yuǎnfāng de péngyou xiěxìn biǎoshì wènhòu.
example.english: He wrote a letter to send greetings to his faraway friend.
example.fact: The Pony Express operated for only about 18 months in 1860-61, yet its riders could carry a letter nearly 3,000 kilometers across the American West in roughly 10 days.

examples.hanzi: 请代我向你父母问候一声。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dài wǒ xiàng nǐ fùmǔ wènhòu yī shēng.
examples.english: Please say hello to your parents for me.

examples.hanzi: 新年到了，大家互相问候，送上祝福。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián dào le, dàjiā hùxiāng wènhòu, sòng shàng zhùfú.
examples.english: With the New Year here, everyone exchanges greetings and good wishes.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 手机的语音助手可以听懂多种语言。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī de yǔyīn zhùshǒu kěyǐ tīngdǒng duōzhǒng yǔyán.
example.english: The phone's voice assistant can understand many languages.
example.fact: In 1952, Bell Labs built "Audrey," one of the earliest machines able to recognize spoken digits, laying groundwork for the voice-recognition systems built into smartphones today.

examples.hanzi: 我在开车，只能给你发语音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài kāichē, zhǐ néng gěi nǐ fā yǔyīn.
examples.english: I'm driving, so I can only send you a voice message.

examples.hanzi: 学外语时，语音是最需要先打好的基础。
examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ shí, yǔyīn shì zuì xūyào xiān dǎhǎo de jīchǔ.
examples.english: When learning a foreign language, pronunciation is the foundation to get right first.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
火 (fire) — marks burning and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 热; 燃 is to burn.
然 (rán) gives the sound exactly: 燃 rán; 然 itself first meant burning, now it means 'so'.

example.hanzi: 一根火柴就能点燃整堆干柴。
example.pinyin: Yī gēn huǒchái jiù néng diǎnrán zhěng duī gānchái.
example.english: A single match can ignite an entire pile of dry firewood.
example.fact: The Centralia mine fire in Pennsylvania was likely ignited by a trash burn in 1962, and the underground coal seam has continued smoldering for more than six decades since.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里点燃了小烟花。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ diǎnrán le xiǎo yānhuā.
examples.english: The children lit small fireworks in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 这场精彩的演讲点燃了大家的热情。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng jīngcǎi de yǎnjiǎng diǎnrán le dàjiā de rèqíng.
examples.english: This brilliant speech ignited everyone's enthusiasm.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 份 is a person's portion or share.
分 (fēn) is a near sound match for fèn; also 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 婚礼上大家都随份子表示祝福。
example.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shàng dàjiā dōu suí fènzi biǎoshì zhùfú.
example.english: At the wedding, everyone chipped in a cash gift to offer their blessings.
example.fact: In imperial China, red envelopes of money called yasuiqian were traditionally given at Lunar New Year to ward off evil spirits, a custom that predates paper currency and once used strings of coins instead.

examples.hanzi: 同事结婚，我随了五百块份子。
examples.pinyin: Tóngshì jiéhūn, wǒ suí le wǔbǎi kuài fènzi.
examples.english: My colleague got married, and I gave a cash gift of five hundred yuan.

examples.hanzi: 过年时，亲戚们都要凑份子请客。
examples.pinyin: Guònián shí, qīnqimen dōu yào còu fènzi qǐngkè.
examples.english: At New Year, the relatives all chip in to host a meal.

components.note: 彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.

example.hanzi: 这家公司给员工提供很好的待遇。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī gěi yuángōng tígōng hěn hǎo de dàiyù.
example.english: This company offers its employees very good treatment and pay.
example.fact: In 1914, Henry Ford doubled the standard wage for his factory workers to five dollars a day, a move that sharply cut turnover and let many employees afford the very cars they were building.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的福利待遇很不错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de fúlì dàiyù hěn bùcuò.
examples.english: This company offers quite good benefits and pay.

examples.hanzi: 他在国外受到了很好的待遇。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guówài shòudào le hěn hǎo de dàiyù.
examples.english: He was treated very well abroad.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 山顶之上是一片辽阔的蓝天。
example.pinyin: Shāndǐng zhīshàng shì yī piàn liáokuò de lántiān.
example.english: Above the mountain peak is a vast expanse of blue sky.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit sits 8,849 meters above sea level, high enough that the air pressure there is only about a third of what it is at sea level.

examples.hanzi: 在法律之上，没有人享有特权。
examples.pinyin: Zài fǎlǜ zhīshàng, méiyǒu rén xiǎngyǒu tèquán.
examples.english: No one is above the law.

examples.hanzi: 飞机飞到了云层之上。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī fēi dào le yúncéng zhīshàng.
examples.english: The plane flew above the clouds.

meanings: to send or receive messages through telecommunications

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 卫星通信让偏远地区也能上网。
example.pinyin: Wèixīng tōngxìn ràng piānyuǎn dìqū yě néng shàngwǎng.
example.english: Satellite communications let even remote areas get online.
example.fact: The first transatlantic telegraph cable, laid in 1858, could carry messages between North America and Europe within minutes, though its insulation failed and the link went dead after barely a month.

examples.hanzi: 以前人们靠写信通信，现在有手机了。
examples.pinyin: Yǐqián rénmen kào xiěxìn tōngxìn, xiànzài yǒu shǒujī le.
examples.english: People used to correspond by letter, but now there are phones.

examples.hanzi: 台风过后，这个地区的通信中断了。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng guòhòu, zhège dìqū de tōngxìn zhōngduàn le.
examples.english: After the typhoon, communications in this area were cut off.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
扌 (hand) — drafting by hand; also in 打 hit, 抄 copy.
以 (yǐ) is only a stand-in for the sound; the traditional 擬 had 疑 yí.

example.hanzi: 飞行员在模拟器里练习紧急降落。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán zài mónǐqì lǐ liànxí jǐnjí jiàngluò.
example.english: The pilot practices emergency landings in the simulator.
example.fact: NASA's so-called "Vomit Comet" simulates weightlessness by flying repeated parabolic arcs, giving astronauts and researchers about 20 to 25 seconds of microgravity on each dive.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件可以模拟真实的考试环境。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ mónǐ zhēnshí de kǎoshì huánjìng.
examples.english: This software can simulate a real exam environment.

examples.hanzi: 下周我们要参加模拟考试。
examples.pinyin: Xià zhōu wǒmen yào cānjiā mónǐ kǎoshì.
examples.english: Next week we're taking a practice exam.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — bows and stretching, as in 弯 bend, 弹 pluck, 引 draw: 张 is to draw a bow.
长 (zhǎng) is a close sound clue for zhāng.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 老鹰张开翅膀从悬崖上飞了出去。
example.pinyin: Lǎoyīng zhāngkāi chìbǎng cóng xuányá shàng fēi le chūqù.
example.english: The eagle spread its wings and flew off the cliff.
example.fact: The wandering albatross has the longest wingspan of any living bird, reaching up to 3.5 meters, letting it glide for hours over open ocean with barely a wingbeat.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝张开嘴，等着妈妈喂饭。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao zhāngkāi zuǐ, děng zhe māma wèi fàn.
examples.english: The baby opened her mouth, waiting for Mom to feed her.

examples.hanzi: 他张开双臂，热情地拥抱了我。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhāngkāi shuāng bì, rèqíng de yōngbào le wǒ.
examples.english: He spread his arms and gave me a warm hug.

components.note: 朿 (cì, a thorn) — two thorns side by side make a thorny shrub; 朿 also appears in 刺 cì.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 这个棘手的问题让整个团队都很头疼。
example.pinyin: Zhège jíshǒu de wèntí ràng zhěnggè tuánduì dōu hěn tóuténg.
example.english: This thorny problem is giving the whole team a headache.
example.fact: The Riemann Hypothesis, proposed in 1859, remains one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems, and the Clay Mathematics Institute still offers a one-million-dollar prize for a proof.

examples.hanzi: 这件事有点棘手，我得想想办法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǒudiǎn jíshǒu, wǒ děi xiǎngxiang bànfǎ.
examples.english: This matter is a bit tricky, so I need to think of a way.

examples.hanzi: 老板交给我一个棘手的任务。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn jiāo gěi wǒ yī gè jíshǒu de rènwu.
examples.english: The boss gave me a thorny task.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 医生提醒他不要过量服用止痛药。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā bùyào guòliàng fúyòng zhǐtòngyào.
example.english: The doctor warned him not to take an excessive dose of painkillers.
example.fact: Water intoxication, though rare, can be fatal — a 2007 radio contest death drew attention to how drinking an excessive amount of water in a short time can dangerously dilute sodium levels in the blood.

examples.hanzi: 过量饮酒对身体不好。
examples.pinyin: Guòliàng yǐnjiǔ duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
examples.english: Drinking excessively is bad for your health.

examples.hanzi: 这种药过量会有副作用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào guòliàng huì yǒu fùzuòyòng.
examples.english: Taking too much of this medicine has side effects.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.hanzi: 孩子紧紧抱住了妈妈的腿。
example.pinyin: Háizi jǐnjǐn bàozhù le māma de tuǐ.
example.english: The child held tightly onto his mother's leg.
example.fact: Tardigrades, microscopic animals nicknamed water bears, survive extreme conditions by curling tightly into a dehydrated ball called a tun, in which their metabolism nearly stops entirely.

examples.hanzi: 她紧紧握着我的手，不愿意放开。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnjǐn wò zhe wǒ de shǒu, bù yuànyì fàngkāi.
examples.english: She held my hand tightly and didn't want to let go.

examples.hanzi: 我们的生活紧紧联系在一起。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de shēnghuó jǐnjǐn liánxì zài yīqǐ.
examples.english: Our lives are closely tied together.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 这次的销售业绩胜过了去年同期。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì de xiāoshòu yèjì shèngguò le qùnián tóngqī.
example.english: This quarter's sales results surpassed the same period last year.
example.fact: In 1954, Roger Bannister became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes, surpassing a barrier many scientists had believed was physiologically impossible.

examples.hanzi: 行动胜过千言万语。
examples.pinyin: Xíngdòng shèngguò qiān yán wàn yǔ.
examples.english: Actions speak louder than words.

examples.hanzi: 这家小店的味道胜过很多大餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā xiǎo diàn de wèidào shèngguò hěn duō dà cāntīng.
examples.english: This little shop's food tastes better than many big restaurants.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — blocking with the hand; also in 挡 block, 推 push.
兰 (lán) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 栏 lán and 烂 làn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 警察拦住了那辆超速行驶的汽车。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá lánzhù le nà liàng chāosù xíngshǐ de qìchē.
example.english: The police stopped the car that was speeding.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was built and rebuilt across many dynasties, with its various sections spanning more than 21,000 kilometers in total, largely to block invasions from northern nomadic groups.

examples.hanzi: 我在门口拦住了正要出去的弟弟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài ménkǒu lánzhù le zhèng yào chūqù de dìdi.
examples.english: I stopped my younger brother at the door as he was about to go out.

examples.hanzi: 一条小河拦住了我们的去路。
examples.pinyin: Yī tiáo xiǎo hé lánzhù le wǒmen de qùlù.
examples.english: A small river blocked our way.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 维多利亚女王统治英国长达六十多年。
example.pinyin: Wéiduōlìyà nǚwáng tǒngzhì Yīngguó chángdá liùshí duō nián.
example.english: Queen Victoria ruled Britain for more than sixty years.
example.fact: Queen Victoria reigned over the United Kingdom for 63 years, from 1837 to 1901, a period so influential that it gave its name to the Victorian era of architecture, literature, and social change.

examples.hanzi: 维多利亚港的夜景非常漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Wéiduōlìyà gǎng de yèjǐng fēicháng piàoliang.
examples.english: The night view of Victoria Harbour is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友在加拿大的维多利亚市工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou zài Jiānádà de Wéiduōlìyà shì gōngzuò.
examples.english: My friend works in Victoria, Canada.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 医生用超声波检查了他腿部的血管。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng chāoshēngbō jiǎnchá le tā tuǐbù de xuèguǎn.
example.english: The doctor used ultrasound to examine the blood vessels in his leg.
example.fact: If all the blood vessels in an adult human body were laid end to end, they would stretch roughly 100,000 kilometers — enough to circle the Earth about two and a half times.

examples.hanzi: 运动可以帮助保持血管健康。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng kěyǐ bāngzhù bǎochí xuèguǎn jiànkāng.
examples.english: Exercise helps keep your blood vessels healthy.

examples.hanzi: 护士很快就找到了他手臂上的血管。
examples.pinyin: Hùshi hěn kuài jiù zhǎodào le tā shǒubì shàng de xuèguǎn.
examples.english: The nurse quickly found the vein in his arm.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.

example.hanzi: 这只赛马拥有纯正的阿拉伯血统。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī sàimǎ yōngyǒu chúnzhèng de Ālābó xuètǒng.
example.english: This racehorse has pure Arabian lineage.
example.fact: Nearly every Thoroughbred racehorse alive today can trace its pedigree back to a small number of foundation sires imported into England in the 17th and 18th centuries, including the influential Darley Arabian.

examples.hanzi: 这只小狗有一半的德国血统。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo gǒu yǒu yībàn de Déguó xuètǒng.
examples.english: This puppy is half German by breed.

examples.hanzi: 他有着中国和法国的混合血统。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuzhe Zhōngguó hé Fǎguó de hùnhé xuètǒng.
examples.english: He is of mixed Chinese and French descent.

components.note: 女 (woman) — marks female relatives and women, as in 妈 mum, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姨 is mother's sister.
夷 (yí) gives the sound exactly: 姨 yí.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 她, 姐, 奶; 妈 is mother.
马 (mǎ) is a close sound clue for mā; also in 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 暑假我要去姨妈家住几天。
example.pinyin: Shǔjià wǒ yào qù yímā jiā zhù jǐ tiān.
example.english: During summer vacation I'm going to stay at my aunt's house for a few days.
example.fact: Many East Asian and Slavic kinship systems, unlike English, use distinct words for a maternal aunt versus a paternal aunt, reflecting how extended-family roles were once tracked more precisely along the maternal and paternal lines.

examples.hanzi: 我姨妈做的红烧肉特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yímā zuò de hóngshāoròu tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The braised pork my aunt makes is especially delicious.

examples.hanzi: 姨妈和妈妈长得很像。
examples.pinyin: Yímā hé māma zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
examples.english: My aunt and my mom look very much alike.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 今后我们要更加注意环保问题。
example.pinyin: Jīnhòu wǒmen yào gèngjiā zhùyì huánbǎo wèntí.
example.english: From now on we need to pay more attention to environmental issues.
example.fact: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, was one of the first international treaties requiring countries to commit to future targets for reducing greenhouse-gas emissions.

examples.hanzi: 今后有问题，随时给我打电话。
examples.pinyin: Jīnhòu yǒu wèntí, suíshí gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: From now on, call me anytime you have a problem.

examples.hanzi: 希望你今后不要再迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Xīwàng nǐ jīnhòu bù yào zài chídào le.
examples.english: I hope you won't be late again in the future.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摆 is to arrange or swing with the hands.
罢 (bà) — near sound — 摆 is bǎi, matching 罢.
平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.

example.hanzi: 他花了很大力气才把这场纠纷摆平。
example.pinyin: Tā huā le hěn dà lìqi cái bǎ zhè chǎng jiūfēn bǎipíng.
example.english: It took him a great deal of effort to settle this dispute.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's praetors served as judicial officials who settled civil disputes, and the structure of that system still shapes the civil-law traditions used across much of continental Europe today.

examples.hanzi: 这件事你放心，我来摆平。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ fàngxīn, wǒ lái bǎipíng.
examples.english: Don't worry about this, I'll sort it out.

examples.hanzi: 经理很快就把客户之间的矛盾摆平了。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ hěn kuài jiù bǎ kèhù zhījiān de máodùn bǎipíng le.
examples.english: The manager quickly settled the conflict between the clients.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 老师鼓励学生们在课堂上多提问。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī gǔlì xuéshēngmen zài kètáng shàng duō tíwèn.
example.english: The teacher encourages students to ask more questions in class.
example.fact: The Socratic method, developed in ancient Athens, teaches by posing a chain of probing questions rather than giving direct answers, and it is still widely used in law schools today.

examples.hanzi: 同学们有问题可以现在提问。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen yǒu wèntí kěyǐ xiànzài tíwèn.
examples.english: Students, you may ask questions now if you have any.

examples.hanzi: 记者向市长提问了三个问题。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě xiàng shìzhǎng tíwèn le sān gè wèntí.
examples.english: The reporter asked the mayor three questions.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metal and money, as in 钱 money, 银 silver.
少 (shǎo) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 抄 chāo, which sounds the same as 钞.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 他从钱包里拿出几张钞票付账。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng qiánbāo lǐ náchū jǐ zhāng chāopiào fùzhàng.
example.english: He took a few bills out of his wallet to pay the bill.
example.fact: The world's first paper money was issued in China during the Tang and Song dynasties, roughly a thousand years before banknotes were adopted in Europe.

examples.hanzi: 他口袋里塞满了皱巴巴的钞票。
examples.pinyin: Tā kǒudài lǐ sāi mǎn le zhòubābā de chāopiào.
examples.english: His pocket was stuffed with crumpled banknotes.

examples.hanzi: 现在很多人都不用钞票，直接用手机付钱。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō rén dōu bù yòng chāopiào, zhíjiē yòng shǒujī fùqián.
examples.english: These days many people don't use cash and just pay with their phones.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
鸟 — the picture of a bird; simplified from 鳥. The bird radical, as in 鸡 chicken, 鸭 duck, 鸽 pigeon.

example.hanzi: 窗台上有一只可爱的小鸟在唱歌。
example.pinyin: Chuāngtái shàng yǒu yī zhī kě'ài de xiǎoniǎo zài chànggē.
example.english: There's a cute little bird singing on the windowsill.
example.fact: The bee hummingbird, native to Cuba, is the smallest bird species in the world, weighing about as much as a U.S. penny and measuring roughly 5 centimeters long.

examples.hanzi: 一只小鸟飞进了教室。
examples.pinyin: Yī zhī xiǎoniǎo fēi jìn le jiàoshì.
examples.english: A little bird flew into the classroom.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在树下喂小鸟吃面包屑。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shù xià wèi xiǎoniǎo chī miànbāoxiè.
examples.english: The children are feeding bread crumbs to the little birds under the tree.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 他是这个领域里知名的专家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zhège lǐngyù lǐ zhīmíng de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is a well-known expert in this field.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize, first awarded in 1901, was funded by dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, who reportedly established it partly to secure a better legacy after mistakenly reading his own obituary.

examples.hanzi: 这位知名作家下个月要来我们学校。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zhīmíng zuòjiā xià gè yuè yào lái wǒmen xuéxiào.
examples.english: This well-known writer will visit our school next month.

examples.hanzi: 她在国内外都是知名的设计师。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài guónèi wài dōu shì zhīmíng de shèjìshī.
examples.english: She is a famous designer both at home and abroad.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 依 is to lean on someone.
衣 (yī) — same sound — 依 is yī, like 衣.
贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赖 is to depend on, or to default on a debt.
剌 (là) hints at the sound: 赖 lài is close, as in 癞 lài and 籁 lài.

example.hanzi: 现代生活越来越依赖智能手机。
example.pinyin: Xiàndài shēnghuó yuè lái yuè yīlài zhìnéng shǒujī.
example.english: Modern life depends more and more on smartphones.
example.fact: Bees and flowering plants depend on each other so closely that roughly one in three bites of food humans eat exists because of pollinators like bees.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不能总是依赖父母。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bù néng zǒngshì yīlài fùmǔ.
examples.english: Children can't always depend on their parents.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的经济依赖旅游业。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de jīngjì yīlài lǚyóuyè.
examples.english: This city's economy depends on tourism.

components.note: 木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.
⺼ (flesh) — the bottom part, the meat/body radical as in 脑, 脚, 胖. Early forms show meat on a bone, but that does not explain 'willing' today.
止 (stop, foot) — the top. Dictionary story: stop 止 flexing muscle ⺼. Memory aid: you stop resisting and agree — 肯定, a hedged mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 林肯是美国历史上最受尊敬的总统之一。
example.pinyin: Línkěn shì Měiguó lìshǐ shàng zuì shòu zūnjìng de zǒngtǒng zhī yī.
example.english: Lincoln is one of the most respected presidents in American history.
example.fact: Abraham Lincoln held eight political debates with Stephen Douglas in 1858, and the widely published exchanges helped propel Lincoln, then a relatively unknown lawyer, toward the presidency two years later.

examples.hanzi: 林肯是我们这次旅行要参观的城市。
examples.pinyin: Línkěn shì wǒmen zhè cì lǚxíng yào cānguān de chéngshì.
examples.english: Lincoln is the city we will visit on this trip.

examples.hanzi: 你知道林肯纪念堂在哪里吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào Línkěn jìniàntáng zài nǎlǐ ma?
examples.english: Do you know where the Lincoln Memorial is?

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — pulling out a thread, hence unraveling; the right part also appears in 译 yì, 释 shì and 泽 zé.

example.hanzi: 侦探通过演绎推理找出了真正的凶手。
example.pinyin: Zhēntàn tōngguò yǎnyì tuīlǐ zhǎochū le zhēnzhèng de xiōngshǒu.
example.english: The detective identified the real culprit through deductive reasoning.
example.fact: Sherlock Holmes, created by Arthur Conan Doyle, is famous for deductive reasoning, though many of his methods are technically closer to abductive inference — reasoning to the most likely explanation rather than pure logical deduction.

examples.hanzi: 这位演员把这个角色演绎得很生动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán bǎ zhège juésè yǎnyì de hěn shēngdòng.
examples.english: This actor portrayed the character very vividly.

examples.hanzi: 这首老歌被年轻歌手重新演绎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu lǎo gē bèi niánqīng gēshǒu chóngxīn yǎnyì.
examples.english: This old song was reinterpreted by a young singer.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
疒 (illness) — marks diseases and cravings, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain.
隐 (yǐn) gives the exact sound; it also means hidden, like a hidden craving.

example.hanzi: 长期玩手机游戏容易让人上瘾。
example.pinyin: Chángqī wán shǒujī yóuxì róngyì ràng rén shàngyǐn.
example.english: Playing phone games for a long time can easily become addictive.
example.fact: Dopamine, a brain chemical linked to reward and motivation, spikes not only when we receive something pleasurable but often in anticipation of it — a mechanism researchers say plays a central role in addictive behavior.

examples.hanzi: 他喝咖啡喝上瘾了，一天不喝就难受。
examples.pinyin: Tā hē kāfēi hē shàngyǐn le, yī tiān bù hē jiù nánshòu.
examples.english: He's hooked on coffee and feels awful if he skips a day.

examples.hanzi: 这部电视剧很容易让人上瘾。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù hěn róngyì ràng rén shàngyǐn.
examples.english: This TV series can easily get you hooked.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops; 穆 first named a ripe grain. Also in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
木 (tree) — two trees side by side make a grove or forest; compare 森 with three.

example.hanzi: 全球有超过十八亿穆斯林信仰伊斯兰教。
example.pinyin: Quánqiú yǒu chāoguò shíbā yì Mùsīlín xìnyǎng Yīsīlánjiào.
example.english: Worldwide, more than 1.8 billion Muslims practice Islam.
example.fact: The Great Mosque of Djenne in Mali, rebuilt in its current form in 1907, is the largest mud-brick building in the world and requires an annual community festival just to replaster its walls after the rainy season.

examples.hanzi: 我的邻居是一位穆斯林，不吃猪肉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū shì yī wèi Mùsīlín, bù chī zhūròu.
examples.english: My neighbor is a Muslim and doesn't eat pork.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅专门为穆斯林顾客提供清真食物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zhuānmén wèi Mùsīlín gùkè tígōng qīngzhēn shíwù.
examples.english: This restaurant serves halal food specially for Muslim customers.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 他常常在夜里工作到很晚。
example.pinyin: Tā chángcháng zài yèli gōngzuò dào hěn wǎn.
example.english: He often works late into the night.
example.fact: Owls have asymmetrical ear openings, with one positioned higher than the other, which lets them pinpoint the exact location of rustling prey in total darkness.

examples.hanzi: 昨天夜里下了一场大雨。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān yèli xià le yī chǎng dàyǔ.
examples.english: It rained heavily last night.

examples.hanzi: 夜里太冷了，记得多盖一床被子。
examples.pinyin: Yèli tài lěng le, jìde duō gài yī chuáng bèizi.
examples.english: It's very cold at night, so remember to use an extra quilt.

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 题, 额, 顺; 顶 is the top of the head, hence any top.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 顶 dǐng is close to 订 dìng and 钉 dīng.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅提供顶级的法国美食。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng tígōng dǐngjí de Fǎguó měishí.
example.english: This restaurant offers top-notch French cuisine.
example.fact: Wagyu beef from Japan's Tajima cattle is graded on a strict marbling scale, and the very top grade, A5, can command prices exceeding $200 per pound at specialty retailers.

examples.hanzi: 这是一款顶级的专业相机。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī kuǎn dǐngjí de zhuānyè xiàngjī.
examples.english: This is a top-of-the-line professional camera.

examples.hanzi: 他请客户去了城里顶级的酒店。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐng kèhù qù le chéng lǐ dǐngjí de jiǔdiàn.
examples.english: He took the client to the city's top hotel.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 朴 is plain, unadorned, as in 朴素 simple.
卜 (bǔ) — close sound: 朴 pǔ. 卜 also sounds out 扑 pū.

example.hanzi: 她穿得很朴素。
example.pinyin: Tā chuān de hěn pǔsù.
example.english: She dresses very simply.
example.fact: 朴 originally meant uncut wood, which explains 朴素 (simple), 朴实 (down-to-earth) and 质朴 (unaffected). It is also a surname, read Piáo (as in Korean Park).

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的装修很朴素。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de zhuāngxiū hěn pǔsù.
examples.english: This restaurant's decor is very plain.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个朴实的农民。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge pǔshí de nóngmín.
examples.english: He is a simple and honest farmer.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 休息几天后，他的气色好多了。
example.pinyin: Xiūxi jǐ tiān hòu, tā de qìsè hǎo duō le.
example.english: After resting for a few days, his complexion looked much better.
example.fact: Human skin's rosy, healthy-looking glow is strongly influenced by blood flow near the surface, which is one reason researchers have found a flushed complexion is consistently rated as more attractive across many cultures.

examples.hanzi: 你今天气色不太好，是不是没睡好？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qìsè bù tài hǎo, shì bu shì méi shuì hǎo?
examples.english: You don't look well today. Did you not sleep well?

examples.hanzi: 奶奶最近气色红润，精神也很好。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuìjìn qìsè hóngrùn, jīngshén yě hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Grandma has a rosy complexion lately and is in good spirits.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 警方还没有查明纵火者的真正意图。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hái méiyǒu chámíng zònghuǒzhě de zhēnzhèng yìtú.
example.english: Police have not yet determined the arsonist's true intent.
example.fact: The FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, formalized in the 1970s, pioneered profiling techniques meant to infer a criminal's intent and psychology from patterns left at a crime scene.

examples.hanzi: 他的意图很明显，就是想骗我们。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yìtú hěn míngxiǎn, jiùshì xiǎng piàn wǒmen.
examples.english: His intention is obvious: he wants to trick us.

examples.hanzi: 我没有意图伤害任何人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu yìtú shānghài rènhé rén.
examples.english: I have no intention of hurting anyone.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 核 is a fruit stone or kernel; 木 marks trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 桌 table.
亥 (hài) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 孩 hái, 咳 ké and 刻 kè.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 地球的核心主要由铁和镍组成。
example.pinyin: Dìqiú de héxīn zhǔyào yóu tiě hé niè zǔchéng.
example.english: Earth's core is made up mainly of iron and nickel.
example.fact: Earth's inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel roughly the size of the Moon, and current estimates put its temperature at about 5,200 degrees Celsius — nearly as hot as the surface of the Sun.

examples.hanzi: 团队合作是这家公司的核心价值。
examples.pinyin: Tuánduì hézuò shì zhè jiā gōngsī de héxīn jiàzhí.
examples.english: Teamwork is this company's core value.

examples.hanzi: 他是球队的核心球员。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì qiúduì de héxīn qiúyuán.
examples.english: He is the core player of the team.

meanings: to work a temporary or casual job

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 很多大学生暑假会去打工赚钱。
example.pinyin: Hěnduō dàxuéshēng shǔjià huì qù dǎgōng zhuànqián.
example.english: Many college students take temporary jobs during summer vacation to earn money.
example.fact: During the Great Depression, teenagers and young adults often took on odd jobs like shining shoes or selling newspapers, work historians now recognize as an early, informal version of today's part-time labor market.

examples.hanzi: 我在餐厅打工，一个小时三十块。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài cāntīng dǎgōng, yī gè xiǎoshí sānshí kuài.
examples.english: I work part-time at a restaurant for thirty yuan an hour.

examples.hanzi: 很多农村人到大城市打工。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō nóngcūn rén dào dà chéngshì dǎgōng.
examples.english: Many rural people go to big cities to work.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 城; hard like packed earth. Top part simplifies 臤 (hard), also in 紧 jǐn and 贤 xián.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 她坚定地拒绝了对方的无理要求。
example.pinyin: Tā jiāndìng de jùjué le duìfāng de wúlǐ yāoqiú.
example.english: She firmly refused the other party's unreasonable demand.
example.fact: Rosa Parks's refusal to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, in 1955 was a firm, deliberate act of civil disobedience that helped ignite the American civil rights movement.

examples.hanzi: 我们要坚定自己的信心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jiāndìng zìjǐ de xìnxīn.
examples.english: We should strengthen our confidence.

examples.hanzi: 他坚定的眼神让我相信他会成功。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiāndìng de yǎnshén ràng wǒ xiāngxìn tā huì chénggōng.
examples.english: His determined gaze made me believe he would succeed.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 这家公司正在开发一款新型电动汽车。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài kāifā yī kuǎn xīnxíng diàndòng qìchē.
example.english: This company is developing a new type of electric car.
example.fact: The Manhattan Project, which developed the first nuclear weapons during World War II, employed more than 130,000 people at its peak and cost roughly $2 billion at the time — equivalent to tens of billions of dollars today.

examples.hanzi: 政府计划开发这片荒地。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jìhuà kāifā zhè piàn huāngdì.
examples.english: The government plans to develop this wasteland.

examples.hanzi: 我们的团队正在开发一个新的手机应用。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de tuánduì zhèngzài kāifā yī gè xīn de shǒujī yìngyòng.
examples.english: Our team is developing a new mobile app.

components.note: 非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.
几 (low table) — the dictionary reads the shape as a plate or stand. Origin of 凡 'all, ordinary' is debated.
丶 (dot) — a small mark inside. 凡 is the sound part of 帆 fān sail and 矾 fán alum; also in 平凡 ordinary. Memory aid: a dot on a plain table.

example.hanzi: 她在音乐方面展现出非凡的才华。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè fāngmiàn zhǎnxiàn chū fēifán de cáihuá.
example.english: She has shown extraordinary talent in music.
example.fact: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart composed his first symphony at age eight, an extraordinarily early display of talent that historians still study for clues about the roots of musical genius.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市在节日里热闹非凡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì zài jiérì lǐ rènao fēifán.
examples.english: The city is extraordinarily lively during the festival.

examples.hanzi: 他有着非凡的记忆力。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuzhe fēifán de jìyìlì.
examples.english: He has an extraordinary memory.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脑 brain, 脚 foot); 脸 is a body part, the face.
佥 (qiān) — loose hint — 脸 is liǎn; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn, 险 xiǎn and 验 yàn, all ending in -ǎn.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，他的脸色瞬间变得苍白。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā de liǎnsè shùnjiān biàn de cāngbái.
example.english: On hearing the news, his complexion instantly turned pale.
example.fact: Blushing, caused by blood vessels near the skin's surface dilating, is a physiological response unique to humans among primates, and Charles Darwin called it "the most peculiar and most human of all expressions."

examples.hanzi: 你脸色这么差，是不是生病了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ liǎnsè zhème chà, shì bu shì shēngbìng le?
examples.english: You look so pale. Are you ill?

examples.hanzi: 老板的脸色一下子沉了下来。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn de liǎnsè yīxiàzi chén le xiàlái.
examples.english: The boss's expression suddenly turned grim.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 休; 倾 is a person leaning over, to tilt or pour out.
顷 (qǐng) hints at the sound: 倾 qīng is close.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.hanzi: 好朋友应该学会倾听彼此的烦恼。
example.pinyin: Hǎo péngyou yīnggāi xuéhuì qīngtīng bǐcǐ de fánnǎo.
example.english: Good friends should learn to listen attentively to each other's troubles.
example.fact: Active listening as a formal counseling technique was popularized by psychologist Carl Rogers in the mid-20th century, who argued that simply reflecting a speaker's feelings back to them could be therapeutically powerful.

examples.hanzi: 她很会倾听，大家都愿意跟她聊天。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì qīngtīng, dàjiā dōu yuànyì gēn tā liáotiān.
examples.english: She is a great listener, so everyone likes chatting with her.

examples.hanzi: 老师耐心地倾听每个学生的想法。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī nàixīn de qīngtīng měi gè xuésheng de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: The teacher patiently listens to every student's ideas.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.hanzi: 科学家从植物中提取出一种天然染料。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā cóng zhíwù zhōng tíqǔ chū yī zhǒng tiānrán rǎnliào.
example.english: Scientists extracted a natural dye from the plant.
example.fact: Aspirin's active compound, salicylic acid, was originally extracted from willow tree bark, a remedy used for pain relief as far back as ancient Egypt and Greece.

examples.hanzi: 他昨天去银行提取了五千块钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuótiān qù yínháng tíqǔ le wǔqiān kuài qián.
examples.english: He went to the bank yesterday and withdrew five thousand yuan.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用密码从自动取款机提取现金。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng mìmǎ cóng zìdòng qǔkuǎnjī tíqǔ xiànjīn.
examples.english: You can withdraw cash from the ATM with a PIN.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 结婚是人生中最重要的好日子之一。
example.pinyin: Jiéhūn shì rénshēng zhōng zuì zhòngyào de hǎorìzi zhī yī.
example.english: Getting married is one of the most important happy days of a person's life.
example.fact: Many traditional Chinese couples still consult the almanac known as the huangli to pick an auspicious wedding date, a practice rooted in centuries-old astrological calendars.

examples.hanzi: 今天是个好日子，我们去领证吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì gè hǎo rìzi, wǒmen qù lǐng zhèng ba.
examples.english: Today is an auspicious day, so let's go register our marriage.

examples.hanzi: 现在我们终于过上了好日子。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài wǒmen zhōngyú guò shàng le hǎo rìzi.
examples.english: Now we are finally living a good life.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips arranged in an even row; 等 means "rank, equal" and then "wait".
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for děng; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 农民要等到秋天才能收获庄稼。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín yào děngdào qiūtiān cáinéng shōuhuò zhuāngjia.
example.english: Farmers have to wait until autumn to harvest their crops.
example.fact: Bristlecone pines, among the oldest living trees on Earth, can go decades between good seed-producing years, a survival strategy suited to the harsh, high-altitude conditions where they grow.

examples.hanzi: 等到你来的时候，我们已经吃完了。
examples.pinyin: Děngdào nǐ lái de shíhou, wǒmen yǐjīng chī wán le.
examples.english: By the time you arrive, we'll have finished eating.

examples.hanzi: 等到春天来了，我们就去郊游。
examples.pinyin: Děngdào chūntiān lái le, wǒmen jiù qù jiāoyóu.
examples.english: When spring comes, we'll go on an outing.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.

example.hanzi: 政府决定加强对网络诈骗的打击力度。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng jiāqiáng duì wǎngluò zhàpiàn de dǎjí lìdù.
example.english: The government decided to strengthen its crackdown on online fraud.
example.fact: After the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, building codes across California were substantially strengthened, requiring structures to better withstand seismic shaking — reforms that shaped modern earthquake engineering.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要加强英语口语的练习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào jiāqiáng Yīngyǔ kǒuyǔ de liànxí.
examples.english: We need to step up our spoken English practice.

examples.hanzi: 学校加强了对学生安全的管理。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào jiāqiáng le duì xuésheng ānquán de guǎnlǐ.
examples.english: The school has tightened its management of student safety.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
氵 (water) — marks water and rivers, as in 河, 海; 源 is the spring where water starts.
原 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 源 yuán, also in 愿 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 笔记本电脑的电源插头突然松动了。
example.pinyin: Bǐjìběn diànnǎo de diànyuán chātóu tūrán sōngdòng le.
example.english: The laptop's power cord plug suddenly came loose.
example.fact: The Hoover Dam, completed in 1936, was for a time the largest hydroelectric power source in the world, and its generators still supply electricity to parts of Nevada, Arizona, and California today.

examples.hanzi: 手机没电了，哪里有电源可以充电？
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī méi diàn le, nǎlǐ yǒu diànyuán kěyǐ chōngdiàn?
examples.english: My phone is dead. Where is there a power outlet to charge it?

examples.hanzi: 修理之前，请先关闭电源。
examples.pinyin: Xiūlǐ zhīqián, qǐng xiān guānbì diànyuán.
examples.english: Please turn off the power before repairing it.

components.note: 珏 (two jades) — here the two 王 shapes suggest strings stretched over a body; 琴 is a string instrument.
今 (jīn) is only a loose sound hint for qín.

example.hanzi: 她每天晚上弹钢琴。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang tán gāngqín.
example.english: She plays the piano every evening.
example.fact: 琴 is the general word for stringed and keyboard instruments: 钢琴 (piano), 小提琴 (violin), 古琴 (guqin). The verbs differ: 弹 for plucked or keyboard instruments, 拉 for bowed ones (拉小提琴).

examples.hanzi: 他从小就学拉小提琴。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xué lā xiǎotíqín.
examples.english: He has been learning the violin since he was little.

examples.hanzi: 我家楼上有人在弹琴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lóu shàng yǒu rén zài tánqín.
examples.english: Someone upstairs from my home is playing an instrument.
